Sources.Title: Mushrooms of our woods
Sources.Intro: A faded poster from the forestry office, pinned by the door. One prized edible, one you must never eat.

Sources.Title: Torn guide page: Boletes
Sources.Intro: A page torn from an old field guide, nailed to the hut wall. Someone has circled one species.

Sources.Title: Field guide: Boletes
Sources.Intro: Pores instead of gills: the cep and its bitter double. Look at the network on the stem and the color of the pores.

Sources.Title: Field guide: Chanterelles and allies
Sources.Intro: Blunt veins, not true gills. The false chanterelle has real, forked gills: check under the cap.

Sources.Title: Field guide: Amanitas
Sources.Intro: The most dangerous group: a ring on the stem and a volva at its base. Always dig up the whole mushroom.

Sources.Title: Field guide: Brittlegills
Sources.Intro: Chalky, brittle flesh that snaps like a stick of chalk; no ring, no volva.

Sources.Title: Field guide: Tricholomas, blewits and spring mushrooms
Sources.Intro: Fleshy gilled mushrooms of the litter and the meadows, from the first spring rings to the last blewits of winter.
